notes: Rows are the test's Rows[32][4] table (buffer_load_dwordx4 into v[4:7]); first4 covers all inputs.

The kernel is 11 independent chunks, each 's_mov_b32 s20, 0; per-lane loop (v_readlane s8..s11 <- v4..v7 of lane s20, SOP1/SOPC/SOPK ops, v_writelane into lane s20 of v10..v25); 4x buffer_store_dwordx4 v[10:25] at offset 64*k'. This is chunk 5 (words [424,491), stores at byte offset 320) = result columns 80..95 in v10..v25; the backward s_cbranch_scc1 at word 490 targets the chunk's first v_readlane (inside the range).

Self-contained: no SGPR is read before being written inside the chunk (s8..s11 from readlane, s20/s30 initialised in the chunk), and v4..v7 are never modified, so running a chunk alone on the oracle matches its run inside the whole kernel.
Columns [92, 93, 94] are Names[]=nullptr (not written by this chunk in the test; the store then repeats the previous chunk's register contents) and not asserted: left out of the column map.
The manifest's alu_word_range [6,80] is chunk 0 only; the manifest's 'non-store instructions between first store and s_endpgm' are the later chunks covered by parts 2..11.

This chunk sets EXEC from the lane's input data (s_mov exec_lo/exec_hi from s9/s10/s11, *_saveexec / *_wrexec) and restores exec_lo=-1 (and exec_hi=0) inside each loop iteration before the next v_writelane, so EXEC is full again at the end of the chunk; no EXEC fix-up needed in post. Columns whose names contain saveexec/wrexec read EXEC: Check() masks them with the host subgroup's lanes only when the host subgroup is narrower than 32; on the wave32 oracle compare with Expected[] unmasked.

64-bit EXEC forms in wave32 (exec_hi writes, *_saveexec_b64) are measured as the hardware does them; the test expects specific exec_hi behaviour for those columns, so a mismatch there is a real finding, not an adapter artifact.
